strack2011_innervated_cohort@1.location: Figure 3D, PDF page 4, filled circles for innervated adult mouse tibialis anterior; caption on page 5
strack2011_innervated_cohort@1.animals: Ten innervated hindlimbs with contralateral denervation
strack2011_innervated_cohort@1.observable: Receptor-associated label remaining relative to the day-7 group mean
strack2011_innervated_cohort@1.timing: Elapsed days from the plotted day-7 normalization point. Horizontal distances were read against the five-day tick spacing.
strack2011_innervated_cohort@1.extraction: Read the centers and end caps on the logarithmic ordinate relative to the initial filled point. Values are approximate whole percentages. The authors' fitted curve was excluded.
strack2011_innervated_cohort@1.uncertainty: The figure caption specifies SD and the methods specify SEM. The bars are recorded without a distributional interpretation. Repeated measurements share the animals and anchor.
strack2011_innervated_cohort@1.interpretation: A labelled cohort is a proxy for surviving surface receptors. Starting on day 7 emphasizes the slow component. The study reports multiple stability classes over the full time course.

devreotes1977_surface_arrival@1.interpretation: The second observation concerns the label among newly inserted receptors. A pool count, fixed transit time and fraction of the original pulse completed cannot be inferred from it.

land1980_receptor_sites_and_current@1.preparation: Esterase-inactivated Anolis intercostal neuromuscular junctions, −100 mV and 23 °C
land1980_receptor_sites_and_current@1.uncertainty: Reported estimated standard errors include systematic error. Condition means combine recordings across muscle fibers. The table does not specify a biological sample count per row.
land1980_receptor_sites_and_current@1.interpretation: The denominator is receptor-rich membrane area. The measured current is the magnitude of a miniature endplate current. Relative binding-site density is a proxy for relative available functional units under an assumed common effective area and single-unit drive.
